title: loom.hook-registry/v1 — the per-repo hook integrity contract the emitter produces
description: Shape of an emitted `.claude/hooks/hook-registry.json`. Consumed by the emitter (`.claude/bin/emit-hook-registry.mjs`), the vendored validator (`.claude/hooks/lib/hook-registry-contract.js::validateManifest`, which loads THIS file rather than restating it) and csq's red tests. THREE FIELD DISCIPLINES, marked per property below: [D] mechanically derived by the emitter from the repo's own registration surfaces; [A] DECLARED BY THE AUTHOR in an `@hook-contract` block comment in the hook file, never a measured value (see `side_effects.declared_by`); [M] MEASURED, and only legal with a named platform + method — omitted entirely when unmeasured, never guessed. This schema checks SHAPE; the cross-field invariants a schema cannot express (content_sha256 recomputes, version major equals the $id major, every row id is the stable derivation of its own row, order is unique per event, a null on_incomplete is only legal where the manifest default and the dispatcher's fail-closed default agree) live in `hook-registry-contract.js::validateManifest` and MUST be run together with this file.

$id.description: The document's identity INCLUDING its major. A consumer that does not know this exact $id MUST refuse the document (see unknown_major_policy) rather than read the fields it recognizes and ignore the rest — a partial read of a contract is how an unknown-major document gets obeyed anyway.

version.description: [D] Semantic version of the emitted document. Its MAJOR MUST equal the $id's major (cross-field check in validateManifest; a mismatch is refused, not warned).

content_sha256.description: [D] sha256 over the CANONICAL JSON of this document with this field removed. Canonicalization is defined in hook-registry-contract.js::canonicalJson (keys sorted at every level, no insignificant whitespace). A consumer recomputes it before trusting any other field — that is what makes the document tamper-evident rather than merely descriptive.

source_sha.description: [D] The 40-hex emitting commit. PER-ROW PROVENANCE IS `hooks[].file_sha256`, NOT THIS FIELD: source_sha names the commit the emit ran against, while a row's file_sha256 pins the bytes that were actually read, so an emitter run over a tree carrying uncommitted hook edits is detectable (the emitter lists the files whose bytes differ from their blob at source_sha on stderr, loudly).

generated_by.description: [D] The emitter that produced this document, as a repo-relative path.

unknown_major_policy.description: [D] Fixed by spec, asserted rather than merely documented: a consumer that meets a $id major it does not implement MUST refuse the document. Emitting anything else would let a forward-compatible-looking manifest be read and obeyed field-by-field.

default_on_incomplete.description: [D] Per-event outcome for a row that does NOT complete: a crash, an own-budget timeout, or a non-zero exit with no JSON reply. PreToolUse is deny because an unanswered permission question must never become an allow; every other event degrades to an advisory miss. A row may override this with its own `on_incomplete`, and `on_crash`/`on_timeout` default to the ROW's value, not to this map.

precedence.const: any deny wins; advise never downgrades a deny
precedence.description: [D] The merge rule a consolidating consumer MUST apply when several rows answer the same event: a single deny refuses the call, and an advisory line from another row never softens it. Fixed text so two consumers cannot implement different merges under one $id.

hooks.description: [D] The registration rows of ONE repo, sorted by (canonical event order, order within the event, then id) so a re-emit over an unchanged tree is byte-identical.

event.description: [D] The host event this row is registered for. An event outside this enum is refused by the emitter, not emitted with a guessed default: the decision semantics of an unknown event cannot be stated, and guessing `continue` is the fail-OPEN direction.

matcher.description: [D] The tool-name matcher this row runs under, or null for EVENT-WIDE. Both a `*` matcher and an omitted matcher normalize to null, because the host treats them identically and a consumer that distinguished them would infer a restriction that is not there.

file.description: [D] Repo-relative path of the hook. Restricted to the top-level hooks tree: everything else under .claude/hooks is a lib the hook loads, and a row pointing at one would give a consumer a dispatch target the host never runs.

file_sha256.description: [D] sha256 of the hook file's EXACT BYTES at emission. This is the field the consumer verifies before dispatching the hook, failing closed on mismatch: a hook whose bytes have moved since the manifest was emitted is not the hook the manifest describes.

id.description: [D] Stable id = sha256(event + "\n" + matcher + "\n" + file), first 16 hex, `hk_` prefix. Deliberately excludes order, timeout and every contract field: an id that moved when a timeout was tuned would be useless as a join key across emissions.

order.description: [D] 1-based position within the row's event — the linearization the dispatcher runs the event's rows in. Unique per event (cross-field check).

on_incomplete.description: [D] The row's own incomplete-run contract, or null to defer to `default_on_incomplete`. A null is only legal where the manifest default and the dispatcher's fail-closed default AGREE (`deny` at PreToolUse); at every other event the emitter REFUSES to emit a null, because the two contracts would read the same null differently — the dispatcher's rule is 'missing means deny' at every event.

on_crash.description: [D] Resolved by the emitter: the row's `on_incomplete` unless the row says otherwise. Emitted concretely rather than left implicit so a consumer never has to re-derive the default chain.

on_timeout.description: [D] Resolved by the emitter: the row's `on_incomplete` unless the row says otherwise.

timeout.description: [D] The row's budget in SECONDS, as the registration surface carries it. null means the surface declares none.

source.description: [D] Where the row came from. loom-template = emitted by the authoring system from its own tree; repo-local = the consuming repo's own registration (`.claude/dispatch-registry.local.json`), which the emitter never writes; third-party = a hook the emitter cannot edit, whose [A] declaration therefore lives in a sibling `<hook>.contract.json` sidecar instead of an in-file block.

surfaces.description: [D] The CLIs whose registration surface references this hook file, derived at FILE level from .claude/settings.json (expanded through dispatch-registry.json), .codex/hooks.json plus the native-policy handler list, and .gemini/settings.json. FILE-level, not matcher-level: a surface naming the file is recorded even when its own tool-name matcher differs from this row's, so a consumer must not read `surfaces` as a per-matcher equivalence claim.

contract.description: Everything a consumer needs to decide whether two rows may share a process, and what the row's answer means once it arrives.

claude.description: [D] cc-hook-json: the payload dispatch.js reads from stdin.

codex.description: [D] codex-hook-json: the dialect after lib/codex-hook-runtime.js normalizes it — the hook itself still reads the CC field names, because the runtime translates at the boundary.

gemini.description: [D] gemini-hook-json: what the Gemini host writes to the hook's stdin.

payload_stdin.description: [D] Per surface: the stdin dialect this row receives. Keyed BY SURFACE because one hook file can be registered on several CLIs and the translation happens outside it.

protocol.description: [D] How the row answers, and what that answer MEANS at its event.

kind.description: [D] Derived from the EVENT, per hook-engine.js § HOST SEMANTICS PER EVENT: PreToolUse=permission-decision, PostToolUse=context-injection, UserPromptSubmit=prompt-gate, Stop/SubagentStop=handback-decision, SessionStart=advisory (exit 2 there is a user-facing error, NOT a refusal), SessionEnd=failure-report, PreCompact=compaction-instructions (raw stdout becomes the instructions). Two rows with different kinds may never be merged into one decision.

exit_codes.description: [D] The LITERAL exit codes present in the hook's source, lexed (comments dropped), sorted, deduped. BLIND SPOT, and it matters: a computed exit (`process.exit(out)`) is NOT represented. Absence of 2 here does NOT mean the row cannot refuse — read `exit_codes_computed` before concluding anything from this array.

exit_codes_computed.description: [D] True when the hook also calls the exit primitive with a non-literal argument, so `exit_codes` is INCOMPLETE for this row. Present as its own field rather than folded into the array so a consumer reading `exit_codes` as `number[]` cannot silently miss the qualifier.

decision_fields.description: [D] The reply keys the hook WRITES, lexed as object keys and member accesses. Blind spots: a reply assembled inside a lib helper, or a computed key, is invisible — an empty array means 'this file constructs no host-read reply field directly', never 'this hook answers nothing'.

severity.description: [D] `block` when the hook's source lexes a refusal token, gated by event — at SessionStart a refusal token is NOT a refusal (the host turns exit 2 into a user-facing error), so such a row is `advise`. Lexed, not grepped: comments and prose are dropped, which is why lib/violation-patterns.js's prose mentions of `severity: "block"` do not count. Cross-checked by .claude/bin/check-deny-capable-declarations.mjs, which owns the drift ratchet between this and the dispatcher's own declaration.

form.description: [D] in-process = the file exports `hookMain`, so the dispatcher can run it in a worker of its own process (the consolidation the consumer wants). legacy = it must be spawned as its own process, whatever else the registry says.

runtime.description: [D] The route the row runs under on the Claude Code lane: `hook-engine-worker` for an in-process row registered through dispatch.js, `node-subprocess` otherwise. The codex lane's extra hop through lib/codex-hook-runtime.js is recorded by `surfaces`, not here.

cwd_scope.description: [D] `process` when the hook's source reads the process working directory anywhere — including a `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd()` fallback, because the entry records what the code CAN depend on, not what it prefers, and a consumer isolating rows must know the fallback exists. `payload` otherwise. Blind spot: a cwd read inside a lib helper the hook calls is not seen here.

side_effects.description: [A] DECLARED BY THE AUTHOR in the hook's `@hook-contract` block (or a sidecar for third-party hooks). Never measured — `declared_by` says so in-band so a consumer cannot mistake a declaration for a measurement. Conservative direction: a conditional capability is declared.

fs_writes.description: [A] Write targets the hook can create, append to, rewrite or delete. Repo-relative POSIX paths; an external target is spelled with a locator prefix from a closed set (`<os.tmpdir()>`, `~`, `<git-common-dir>`, `<npm-cache>`, `<sibling-worktree-path>`, `<main-checkout>`, `<edited-file>`). Runtime-dependent segments are `<placeholders>`. SHAPE ONLY — the emitter validates the entry's form and locator name, never that the path is really written.

network.description: [A] True when the hook's OWN process opens a socket/DNS/HTTP connection. A spawned child that reaches the network is covered by `spawns`, not here.

spawns.description: [A] True when the hook starts another process, directly or through a lib helper. This is the flag that most often forbids merging two rows into one worker: a child's process semantics and timeout are its own, not the host's.

declared_by.description: [A] Constant, emitted by the emitter, never written by hand: the manifest's own marker that these values are a declaration.

idempotent.description: [A] True when re-running the row with the same payload leaves the durable state unchanged (a repeat makes no further write). The decision MAY differ only as a consequence of state the first run changed — a consumed one-shot receipt is therefore NOT idempotent. Declared by the author, never measured.

cost.description: [M] MEASURED cost, present ONLY when actually measured. A partial or guessed cost FAILS the emit (the authoring contract says omit it entirely rather than estimate), so a consumer may treat the presence of this object as a measurement and its absence as unknown — never as zero. The emitter supplies no cost today.

platform.description: [M] The machine, CI image or OS the numbers were taken on. A cost with no named platform is not comparable and is refused rather than recorded.

method.description: [M] How it was measured (the harness/command), so a reader can judge whether the number applies to their situation.
